title: Normalized affine global-section compositors
statement: Use [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections] for A-valued ordinary sections Γ_{X,A}, derived sections G_X, and their fixed universal derived units. Retain its data S,A,Y≅Spec A,X,f:X→Y, and the original compatible-chart direct image f_* and its derived functor Rf_* [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]. The structure modules on the full and small sites are identified by the canonical restriction-of-unit isomorphism. Its inverse, followed by the existing restriction equivalence [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], extends a small-site section to every full scheme chart. Define the ordinary compositor Γ_{X,A}≅Γ_{Y,A}f_* as the unique natural isomorphism with this formula: for a section s, a target chart V, a chart q of X over V and b∈O_Y(V), the q-projection of the image section, evaluated on b, is the extended s on q evaluated on the pullback of b. Define the derived compositor κ:G_X≅G_Y Rf_* as the unique natural isomorphism whose square with the universal derived units on every cochain complex is the termwise ordinary compositor followed by the G_Y-image of the Rf_* derived unit. This is an isomorphism by the usual K-injective/global-section acyclicity composition argument. Define A→Γ_{Y,A}(O_Y) by a↦a·id_{O_Y}; it is an isomorphism. Its image on degree-zero complexes, followed by the universal derived-sections unit and the canonical single-complex localization comparisons, gives A\lbrack 0\rbrack→G_Y(O_Y). Affine etale quasi-coherent acyclicity makes this insertion an isomorphism; define G_Y(O_Y)≅A\lbrack 0\rbrack as its inverse. These ordinary and derived compositors and affine structure isomorphism use actual sections and units, rather than an unspecified natural isomorphism.
